stories.headline: Iran Fires on 3 Ships in Strait of Hormuz and Seizes 2 as US Blockade and Ceasefire Both Continue

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired on three commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz on April 22 and seized two of them (MSC Francesca and Epaminondas), intensifying its assault on shipping in the waterway.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran fired on three ships in the Strait of Hormuz and seized two of them Wednesday, intensifying its assault on shipping in the key waterway.

key_facts.fact: The attacks came hours after Trump extended the ceasefire while maintaining the US naval blockade; Treasury Secretary Bessent said Kharg Island storage will soon be full and Iranian oil wells will be shut in.
key_facts.excerpt: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wrote on social media that under Trump's orders, the U.S. Navy will continue the blockade of Iran's ports. 'In a matter of days, Kharg Island storage will be full and the fragile Iranian oil wells will be shut in.'

key_facts.fact: Brent crude briefly surpassed $100/barrel, a 35% increase from prewar levels; the standoff has choked off nearly all exports through the strait where 20% of the world's traded oil passes in peacetime.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures with June delivery traded 0.5% higher at $99.03 per barrel, paring gains after briefly surpassing $100.

key_facts.fact: Iran refused to send a delegation to a second round of peace talks in Pakistan; its chief negotiator said a ceasefire 'only makes sense' if not violated by the US blockade.
key_facts.excerpt: Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, Iran's parliament speaker who met with U.S. Vice President JD Vance in Pakistan earlier this month, said a complete ceasefire 'only makes sense' if it is not violated by the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports.

key_facts.fact: The US has turned back 31 vessels since its blockade began on April 13; there have been more than 30 attacks on ships in the Mideast since the war started February 28.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. has turned back 31 vessels since its blockade began, U.S. Central Command said Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Panama condemned the 'illegal seizure' of the Panama-flagged MSC Francesca, calling it a serious attack on maritime security; the White House said seizures didn't violate ceasefire terms.
key_facts.excerpt: Panama condemned what it called the 'illegal seizure' of the Panama-flagged MSC Francesca, and said it represented a serious attack on maritime security.

stories.headline: SK Hynix Posts Record Q1: Revenue Tops 50T Won for First Time, 72% Operating Margin Surpasses Nvidia

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix reported Q1 operating profit of 37.61 trillion won ($27.8B), five times higher than a year earlier, and record revenue of 52.58 trillion won ($38.9B), up 198% YoY — the first time quarterly revenue surpassed 50 trillion won.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue also hit a record 52.58 trillion won ($38.9 billion), up 198 percent from the same period a year earlier. It is the first time SK hynix's quarterly revenue has surpassed 50 trillion won.

key_facts.fact: Operating margin reached 72%, surpassing Nvidia's semiconductor industry peak of 65% (Q4 2025) and TSMC's 58.1% (Q1 2026), an unprecedented level for an asset-heavy memory manufacturer.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix's 72% operating margin not only exceeded the semiconductor industry peak of 65% set by Nvidia in the fourth quarter of 2025, but also significantly outperformed TSMC's 58.1% operating margin in the first quarter of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The average price of DRAM used in HBM jumped to $13/unit at end of Q1, ten times the $1.35 of a year earlier; SK Hynix held a 57% share of the HBM market.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung managed to reclaim the top spot in DRAM revenue in the last three months of 2025, according to data from Counterpoint Research, though SK Hynix continued to dominate in HBM with a 57% market share.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said HBM demand will exceed its production capacity for the next three years; the company plans to ship HBM4E samples in H2 2026 and begin mass production in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: 'HBM demand required over the next three years exceeds our production capacity,' SK hynix said.

key_facts.fact: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won reportedly said in March that the global chip wafer shortage is likely to persist until 2030, with a projected shortfall exceeding 20%.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won reportedly stated in March 2026 that the global chip wafer shortage is likely to persist until 2030, as demand for HBM continues to outpace supply.

stories.headline: Wall Street's 6 Largest Banks Cut 15,000 Jobs in Q1 Citing AI While Posting $47B in Combined Profit

key_facts.fact: The six largest Wall Street banks — JPMorgan Chase, Citi, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and Wells Fargo — collectively eliminated 15,000 positions in Q1 2026 while posting combined profits of $47 billion, an 18% increase YoY.
key_facts.excerpt: The six banks collectively eliminated 15,000 positions in Q1, while posting combined profits of $47 billion, an 18 percent increase over the previous year.

key_facts.fact: Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan reversed his earlier assurance that AI posed no threat to jobs, announcing the bank shed 1,000 positions through attrition by 'eliminating work and applying technology.'
key_facts.excerpt: Less than four months after assuring the bank's 210,000 employees in a television interview that AI posed no threat to their jobs, Moynihan announced the bank had shed 1,000 positions through attrition by 'eliminating work and applying technology.'

key_facts.fact: Citi committed to reducing its workforce by 20,000 employees through what it calls a 'productivity and efficiency journey,' using AI software from Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: Citi has committed to reducing its workforce by 20,000 employees through what executives describe as a 'productivity and efficiency journey.' The bank utilizes AI software from Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: AI is being deployed across banking to automate paperwork compliance, account opening approvals, invoice generation, legal document review, and organization of sensitive customer data.
key_facts.excerpt: The applications of AI in banking span from back-office operations to front-office professional work, with banks using it to process paperwork compliance, account opening approvals, invoice generation, legal document review, and organization of sensitive customer data.

key_facts.fact: Some 80,000 tech workers were laid off in Q1 2026, with 47.9% attributed to AI and automation according to Nikkei Asia; even Sam Altman admitted there is 'AI washing' where companies blame AI for layoffs they planned anyway.
key_facts.excerpt: 78,000 tech jobs gone in three months. 76% of them in the US. Nikkei Asia says 47.9% were attributed to AI and automation.

stories.headline: EU Launches AccelerateEU Strategy to Slash Fossil Fuel Dependence After €24B Iran War Energy Shock

key_facts.fact: The European Commission launched AccelerateEU, a new strategy to reduce fossil fuel dependence and shield the bloc from energy price shocks; the EU has spent an additional €24 billion on energy imports since the Iran war escalation without receiving any extra energy.
key_facts.excerpt: 'Since the escalation of the conflict in the Middle East, the EU has spent an additional €24 billion on energy imports due to higher prices – without receiving a single extra molecule of energy,' the European Commission said.

key_facts.fact: The Commission will avoid major market interventions like gas price caps or windfall taxes for now; instead it plans to curb EU tax rules to favour electricity over oil and gas, and make it easier for governments to cut industrial electricity taxes to zero.
key_facts.excerpt: Draft proposals seen by Reuters show the EU will, for now, avoid major market interventions such as capping gas prices or taxing energy companies' windfall profits. Instead, the Commission plans to curb EU tax rules to favour electricity over oil and gas.

key_facts.fact: EU energy commissioner Dan Jørgensen warned the disruption is costing Europe around €500 million per day; the Commission will present an Electrification Action Plan by summer with a binding electrification target.
key_facts.excerpt: Crucially, the Commission will present legislative proposals on network charges and taxation in May, so electricity is taxed less than gas. Next to that, the Commission will present an Electrification Action Plan by the Summer which will include an electrification target.

key_facts.fact: The EU produced 71% of its electricity from low-carbon sources (renewables + nuclear) in 2025, up from ~60% in 2022, which analysts say makes the electricity price shock smaller than in 2022 despite the oil shock potentially being worse.
key_facts.excerpt: The EU produced 71% of its electricity from low-carbon sources, including renewables and nuclear, last year, up from around 60% in 2022, data from think tank Ember showed.

key_facts.fact: Von der Leyen said: 'We must accelerate the shift to homegrown, clean energies. This will give us energy independence and security, and mean we are better able to weather geopolitical storms.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We must accelerate the shift to homegrown, clean energies. This will give us energy independence and security and mean we are better able to weather geopolitical storms.'

stories.headline: Germany Unveils First-Ever Military Strategy, Aims to Be Europe's Strongest Conventional Army by 2029

key_facts.fact: Germany's Chief of Defence General Carsten Breuer signed the Bundeswehr's first Military Strategy on April 22, forming the Overall Concept for Military Defence; the full document is classified.
key_facts.excerpt: General Carsten Breuer, the Bundeswehr's Chief of Defence, today signed Germany's first Military Strategy (Militärstrategie der Bundeswehr).

key_facts.fact: The strategy targets 460,000 total soldiers (260,000 active, 200,000 reserve) by mid-2030s, with an interim milestone of 204,000 active soldiers by 2029, up from ~186,000 today.
key_facts.excerpt: German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius said Berlin aimed for a military of 460,000 soldiers, a target set in 2025 that includes 200,000 reservists.

key_facts.fact: Russia is identified as the 'greatest and most direct threat' to German and transatlantic security; the strategy states 'Russia is creating the conditions for a military attack on NATO countries.'
key_facts.excerpt: In military strategy, Russia is considered for the foreseeable future to be the 'greatest and most direct threat' to German and transatlantic security.

key_facts.fact: Priority capabilities include air defence, long-range precision strikes across all domains, territorial missile defence, and AI integration; the strategy introduces a 'One-Theatre-Approach' connecting domains.
key_facts.excerpt: Germany will develop the capability to conduct deep precision strikes across all domains and to provide territorial missile defence.

key_facts.fact: Defence Minister Pistorius said: 'Our ambition is and must be to be Europe's strongest conventional military,' noting that AI and automation will impact troop planning and qualifications.
key_facts.excerpt: 'It is clear that automation and artificial intelligence will continue to impact our planning, how many troops we will need and with what qualifications,' he noted. 'Our ambition is and must be...to be Europe's strongest conventional military.'

stories.headline: Samsung Union Rally Draws 30,000+ Workers Demanding 15% of AI Chip Profits, Threatens 18-Day Strike

key_facts.fact: Police estimated 30,000 attendees (organizers said 39,000-40,000) at the rally outside Samsung's Pyeongtaek semiconductor complex — the largest union rally in Samsung's history.
key_facts.excerpt: Police told local media about 30,000 people attended the rally in South Korea's southern city of Pyeongtaek, home to Samsung's sprawling semiconductor complex, while organizers put the number at 39,000.

key_facts.fact: The union demands 15% of operating profit be allocated to chip-division employees; the total would exceed 40 trillion won ($27B), or more than $400,000 per worker on average.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung's labor union wants 15% of operating profit handed to chip-division employees. The figure — more than 40 trillion won ($27 billion) — could mean more than $400,000 per worker on average.

key_facts.fact: Workers threaten an 18-day general strike starting May 21 if demands are not met; this could delay chip deliveries to customers and further push up memory prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Si leurs revendications ne sont pas satisfaites, ils prévoient de faire grève pendant 18 jours à partir du 21 mai.

key_facts.fact: The core grievance is a massive bonus gap with rival SK Hynix: a Samsung chip worker with a ₩76M base salary reportedly received ₩38M in bonuses for 2025, less than one-third what an SK Hynix employee with similar pay would get.
key_facts.excerpt: Le syndicat des travailleurs de Samsung Electronics affirme qu'un employé de la division des puces, dont le salaire de base est de 76 millions de wons, recevrait 38 millions de wons de prime pour 2025, soit moins d'un tiers du montant auquel un employé de SK Hynix bénéficiant d'un salaire similaire pourrait prétendre.

key_facts.fact: Union membership has surged past 90,000, representing over 70% of Samsung's South Korean workforce; management proposed 10% of operating profit for performance pay and a 6.2% wage increase but rejected abolishing the bonus cap.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics says it has proposed a compensation package to the union that includes a 6.2% wage increase, special compensation and expanded benefits...maintaining a negative position on the union's demand to abolish the cap on performance bonuses.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Denali's Avlayah, First Biologic Designed to Cross Blood-Brain Barrier, for Hunter Syndrome

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval for Avlayah (tividenofusp alfa-eknm), the first FDA-approved biologic specifically designed to cross the blood-brain barrier, for treatment of neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome (MPS II).
key_facts.excerpt: Denali Therapeutics Inc. announced the FDA has granted accelerated approval for Avlayah (tividenofusp alfa-eknm), the first FDA-approved biologic specifically designed to cross the blood-brain barrier and reach the whole body, including the brain.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase I/II clinical trial, Avlayah demonstrated a 91% reduction in cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate (CSF HS) levels from baseline by week 24; 93% of patients (41 of 44) had CSF HS levels within the range of individuals without Hunter syndrome.
key_facts.excerpt: In a Phase I/II clinical trial, Avlayah demonstrated a 91% (95% CI: 89%, 92%) reduction in CSF HS levels from baseline by week 24 of treatment. At week 24, 93% (41 of 44) of Avlayah-treated patients had CSF HS levels within the range of individuals without Hunter syndrome.

key_facts.fact: The approval validates Denali's TransportVehicle platform for delivering biologic medicines across the blood-brain barrier, potentially applicable to a wide range of neurodegenerative diseases and lysosomal storage disorders.
key_facts.excerpt: 'This milestone validates our TransportVehicle platform and its potential to overcome the long-standing challenge of delivering biologic medicines across the blood-brain barrier, with the aim to transform the treatment of a wide range of neurodegenerative diseases, lysosomal storage disorders and other serious diseases.'

key_facts.fact: Hunter syndrome affects approximately 1 in 100,000 to 170,000 male births; existing therapies like Elaprase cannot reach the brain. Avlayah is the first therapeutic innovation for the community in nearly 20 years.
key_facts.excerpt: 'The FDA approval of Avlayah represents a breakthrough advance as the first therapeutic innovation for the Hunter syndrome community in nearly 20 years.'

key_facts.fact: Continued approval may be contingent upon verification of clinical benefit in the Phase II/III COMPASS confirmatory trial, currently enrolling participants in North America, South America, and Europe.
key_facts.excerpt: Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial.
